tob-10784: C. J. S. Thompson’s richly illustrated history traces alchemy from ancient Egypt through the medieval adepts to the birth of modern chemistry and pharmacy. The book captures the romance of a science that was half magic and half experiment.
tob-4184: Diogenes Laertius is our tale-bearer of Greek thought — his Lives keep the quips, habits, and teachings of all, from Thales to Epicurus. Without him we would know far less of the old sages. C. D. Yonge’s rendering brings this needful, ever-amusing storehouse to English readers.
tob-4284: Budge’s Book of the Dead musters the Egyptian charms for threading the underworld — the pleas before the two-and-forty judges, the words of power, the charts of the night. His rendering, long the standard, made the papyri speak plain. The book is old Egypt’s handbook for forever.
tob-4161-70484: The second volume of Tylor’s Primitive Culture turns to tale, rite, and wonder-working — showing how rites and stories spell early man’s reading of the world. His matching way set the mold for man-lore. The two books together stay the field’s founding text.
tob-0184: G. R. S. Mead’s book gives the Hymn of the Pearl — the Gnostic song of a prince who sinks into Egypt to win a pearl, forgetting then minded of his kingly birth. Few soul-parables sing so fair. Mead’s Englishing and gloss light its deeps.
tob-14184: R. H. Charles’s Old Testament Cast-Out Books muster the uncanon’d books in clear English. His learned Englishings, with notes and fore-words, made these olden texts open to all. Scholars still start here. The gathering stays the standard English handbook for the field.
arxiv-2605-08784: Online stores need endless product posters, and AI-generated advertising art is becoming the cheap way to make them. Benlei Cui and eight coauthors offer SIMPLEPOSTER, a deliberately plain baseline for automatic poster generation. The point of the 2026 paper is honesty in comparison: by showing what a no-frills method achieves, it gives every fancier approach something solid to beat.
arxiv-2605-08884: Ricci shrinkers are special shapes that evolve under Ricci flow by simply shrinking — they model how singularities form in geometry. Pak-Yeung Chan and Yongjia Zhang prove rigidity and gap theorems for them, showing these shapes are far more constrained than they look. The 2026 paper is pure differential geometry on the anatomy of singularities.
arxiv-2605-08984: FPGAs reconfigure themselves from bitstreams, and a malicious one can hijack the hardware. Rye Stahle-Smith, Carter Antley, Jason D. Bakos, and colleagues screen bitstreams at line rate — as fast as they arrive — using hardware acceleration. The 2026 paper is hardware security: inspecting the goods before the gates open.
arxiv-2605-09184: Ontologies — formal maps of what exists in a domain — are painful to build and merge by hand. Fabio Rovai proposes open ontologies: tool-augmented engineering with stable matching alignment to reconcile competing maps. The 2026 paper is knowledge representation with algorithmic diplomacy.
arxiv-2605-09284: Mesh-based simulations — weather, airflow — are accurate only on fine meshes, which cost dearly. Jiyeon Kim, Youngjoon Hong, and Won-Yong Shin bring neural super-resolution to the rescue, sharpening coarse simulations with semi-supervised learning. The 2026 paper gets fine-mesh accuracy on a coarse-mesh budget.
arxiv-2605-09384: Doctors asking questions about medical images need AI that reasons step by step — chain of thought — without retraining giants. Runze Ma, Shunbo Jia, Haonan Lyu, and colleagues adapt efficiently with LiteMedCoT-VL. The 2026 paper is medical visual question answering on a budget.
arxiv-2605-09584: Hospital inpatients need decisions supported by open-ended reasoning, not multiple choice. Aishik Nagar, Arun-Kumar Kaliya-Perumal, Yu-Hsuan Han, and colleagues reinforce that reasoning with outcome-aware rubrics — CLR-voyance. The 2026 paper is clinical AI for the ward.
arxiv-2605-09684: AI agents need monitors watching them, and those monitors themselves need red-teaming. Monika Jotautaitė, Maria Angelica Martinez, Ollie Matthews, and colleagues build MonitoringBench: semi-automated red-teaming for agent monitoring. The 2026 paper tests the watchers before the watched misbehave.
arxiv-2605-09884: The moon's cratering is asymmetric — one face bears more scars — and lunar ejecta may be the missing piece resolving the puzzle. Hailiang Li, Xiaoping Zhang, and Li-Yong Zhou make the case. The 2026 paper is planetary science on the moon's lopsided history.
arxiv-2605-09984: 4D generation — three dimensions plus time — needs grounding in physical reality; geometric 4D stitching provides it. Sunwoo Park, Taesung Kwon, and Jong Chul Ye develop the stitching method. The 2026 paper is generative 4D, stitched to the ground. It grounds generated worlds in geometry.
arxiv-2605-10084: Audio representations disentangled by power for generative modeling — PoDAR separates loudness from content. arxiv-2605-10384: Agentic AI at the edge — performance insights from rigorous benchmarking. Shiqiang Wang and Herbert Woisetschläger provide the measurements. The 2026 paper is edge AI evaluation. It benchmarks how agentic AI precisely when deployed at the edge. Edge benchmarking truly matters.
pmc-13447184: TriageHF heart-failure monitoring in real-world practice — the limits of assuming no news is good news. Masataka Kawana examines the data. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is cardiology. It questions silence as a sign of stability. Silence is not safety.
pmc-13405084: Physical activity during COVID-19 confinement — cluster profiles of its barriers and facilitators, found with machine learning in a cross-sectional study. pmc-13403884: Periodontitis metabolites — precisely profiled on a detection platform of mesoporous gold-chromium oxide particles with Schwarz P surface. pmc-13579584: Introducing solid foods to infants — caregivers' beliefs, readiness, and influences on feeding practices, qualitatively explored. arxiv-2606-16984: From the 911 call to the hospital door, this paper maps where artificial intelligence could genuinely help emergency medical services, and where it could hurt. arxiv-2606-17084: Kostas Tzanavaris revisits the perfect fluid, the idealized matter that fills textbook cosmology, through the action principle, the deep rule that nature extremizes a quantity called the action. arxiv-2606-17284: Kuantay Boshkayev and colleagues compute the shadow, emission, and strong-field lensing of dilatonic black holes, which carry an extra scalar field beyond Einstein's theory. arxiv-2606-17384: Ahmad Darkhalil, Dima Damen, and David Fouhey improve and evaluate hand-object interaction detection. arxiv-2606-17784: Aimeric Colléaux and colleagues study quasi-topological gravity in exotic spacetimes: Taub-NUT, near-horizon extreme Kerr, and swirling geometries. arxiv-2606-17884: Christian Böhning and colleagues exhibit naive atoms of blowups through examples. arxiv-2606-17984: Andrés Plazas Malagón and colleagues calibrate Planck Sunyaev-Zel'dovich cluster masses with weak lensing from HSC-SSP Year 3. arxiv-2606-18184: S. D. Campos goes beyond plane waves to study coherent network response to collimated gravitational-wave wavepackets. plos-pone-0003384: Cell biologists probed a gene-silencing protein's quieter role in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003484: Behavioral ecologists documented deadly romance paying off in this 2008 field study. plos-pone-0003584: Botanists proved museum drawers hold readable DNA in this 2008 methods paper. plos-pone-0003684: In 2008, Tricco, Brehaut, and Chen audited the Cochrane review pipeline. plos-pone-0003784: Halpern, Ogunsola, and Obunge tested a vaginal gel against HIV in this 2008 trial. The phase II study measured whether 6 percent cellulose sulfate gel could block male-to-female HIV transmission. The trial put a much-hoped prevention tool to a rigorous test.
plos-pone-0003884: In 2008, Kent and Meredith found potassium channels keeping the brain's clock ticking. BK channels regulated the rhythmic firing of neurons in the suprachiasmatic nucleus, the body's master pacemaker. The result ties daily rhythms to the electrical beat of clock cells.
plos-pone-0003984: In 2008, Ben-Simon, Podlipsky, and Arieli found the resting brain double-booked. Two distinct alpha-rhythm processes ran at once in the supposedly idle brain. plos-pone-0004084: In 2008, a Spanish team tested handouts for a dying vulture. Supplementary feeding aimed to lift the endangered vulture's odds. The team weighed the practice's power to boost population viability. Feeding stations emerged as a practical lifeline for the hungry birds.

plos-pone-0004584: In 2009, Morlan, Baker, and Sinicropi built a sharper mutation sniffer. Mutation detection by real-time PCR offered a simple, robust, highly selective method. The test spotted rare mutants fast. The method aids cancer diagnosis today. The neat approach is highly practical.
plos-pone-0004684: In 2009, He, Gitschier, and Zerjal mapped where HapMap volunteers' ancestors lived long ago. Geographical affinities of the HapMap samples were charted. plos-pone-0358184: Carbon-ion therapy demands precise stopping-power maps to hit tumors and spare healthy tissue. plos-pone-0357784: The sharing economy promises opportunity for all — but the reality is uneven. This qualitative text analysis from focus groups explored digital inequalities in the sharing economy. plos-pone-0357984: Dialysis patients accumulate indoxyl sulfate — a gut-derived toxin that inflames blood vessels. plos-pone-0343484: Indigenous Ethiopian zebu cattle endure heat that would fell imported breeds. plos-pone-0357384: Exercise sharpens adolescent minds — partly by quieting rumination, partly through mindfulness. plos-pone-0356884: A questionnaire measuring social determinants of health is only useful if it means the same thing everywhere. plos-pone-0354384: Nurse turnover bleeds hospitals dry — and predicting it could staunch the flow. This paper published a protocol for a systematic review of prediction models for nurse turnover. plos-pone-0356684: Fiber-optic cables on coal shearers endure brutal heat underground. This paper characterized the temperature characteristics of fiber-optic shearer cables. The thermal data help engineers design cables that survive the mine’s inferno while carrying critical signals.
plos-pone-0355984: Autism’s biology remains elusive — but big data may crack it. plos-pone-0356784: Malnutrition wears two faces in Panama: undernutrition and obesity side by side. plos-pone-0356284: Studying retinal degeneration needs mouse models that mimic both slow and fast human disease. plos-pone-0350484: How does a dolphin hear so exquisitely? plos-pone-0354884: Women carrying BRCA1/2 mutations face agonizing family planning decisions. plos-pone-0355784: The words we choose for family — kinship terms — are tangled up with grammar itself. This paper argued that word choice is coupled with grammar through the case of kinship. plos-pone-0356384: A fungus living inside plants — Aspergillus fumigatus as an endophyte — can shield okra from salt and cadmium. plos-pone-0335384: China’s Qinling mountains — a biodiversity treasure — need soil health monitoring. This paper assessed soil quality using TDS and MDS indicator methods. plos-pone-0326984: An old ankle sprain changes how you squat — in subtle, measurable ways. plos-pone-0353484: China’s hospital labs handle Streptococcus pneumoniae daily — but practices vary wildly. plos-pone-0355284: CD93 — a cell surface protein — may drive stomach cancer’s growth and blood supply. plos-pone-0355684: Ethiopian women’s access to treatment for obstetric complications splits along the urban-rural divide. plos-pone-0355484: Ireland needs nurse managers — but what makes nurses aspire to lead? This paper identified the key predictors of nurse management aspirations. plos-pone-0355384: Fragile X disorders go undiagnosed in Nigerian children — but public health screening could change that. plos-pone-0347184: Eating disorders hide in primary care — and screening must be validated. This scoping review — focused on adolescents and adults — mapped validated screening strategies. plos-pone-0353684: Thyroid nodules on ultrasound — segmenting them accurately guides biopsies. PM-DUnet fuses long-range dependencies and attention in a dual-U architecture for that segmentation. plos-pone-0354184: Ischemic stroke — treated with simvastatin delivered by platelet-mimicking nanoparticles. This paper built that biomimetic targeted delivery system. plos-pone-0352784: Post-stroke depression in Tanzania — its predictors and evolution. This protocol outlines a prospective study of adults admitted for first stroke at Dodoma referral hospitals. plos-pone-0354484: Ethiopian nurses’ work-related musculoskeletal disorders — their epidemiology synthesized. This systematic review and meta-analysis did so. plos-pone-0352184: Oman’s mental health continuum — measured validly in Arabic. This paper validated the Arab Mental Health Continuum Short Form’s psychometric properties and factorial structure. plos-pone-0353784: Runners breathing through respirator-restricted airways — respiratory patterns by sex. This paper measured the changes in female and male runners. plos-pone-0353184: Estonian STI clinic attendees — their risk profiles identified. This paper did so. The profiling revealed distinct behavioral clusters among those seeking testing. plos-pone-0353284: Western Kenyan children with cancer — asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 exposure estimated from serological data. This retrospective analysis did so. plos-pone-0353384: Generative AI fitness assistants — intention to use determined by planned behavior theory, system quality, and perceived factors. This paper integrated them. plos-pone-0352384: Milk pasteurization — a solar-assisted venturi-plasma system simulated and performance-analyzed. This paper did so. The design pairs sunlight with plasma physics to kill pathogens. plos-pone-0352684: Granite-weathered soil — compaction energy and moisture effects on permeability and compression. This paper studied the influence. plos-pone-0352584: Moral foundations — age, gender, and score distributions. This paper mapped them. The analysis showed how morality’s pillars vary demographically. Its finding is descriptive. plos-pone-0352984: Early trabecular changes around implants — evaluated by fractal analysis and panoramic indices. This paper did so. The method reads bone texture around the implant. Its clinical value is early warning. The work watches the bone embrace — or reject — the implant.

plos-pone-0351884: Elite taekwondo athletes — three warm-up protocols’ acute effects on drop jump biomechanics, IMU-analyzed. This paper tested them. europmc-pmc2819884: A rare but deadly fungal infection was rising in France, and this 2009 paper quantifies the trend.
